_comment: keep-raw decisions for iznik-routing-go, per plan section 7.4/7.5
(plans/database-migration-evaluation-2026-07.md).
This service does not import gorm.io/gorm (confirmed against go.mod and by
grepping the tree) - it talks to MySQL purely via database/sql. Scoping
found zero sites in waves 1-3 (single-table SELECT/write/upsert) and only
two in wave 4 (multi-table SELECT, no MySQL-only functions); the other 11
are spatial predicates or fully dynamic runtime-built queries - the exact
shapes plan 7.5 already keeps raw elsewhere. That is not enough mechanical
surface to justify adding a GORM dependency and the 4-layer parity harness
to a service that has neither today, so every site here is keep-raw rather
than raw/in-progress. See tools/orm-migration/README.md and the scoping
report in the team's session history for the full reasoning.
Every site in this service is a real MySQL statement against the migrated
database (unlike iznik-spatial-go, which also has 'not applicable' sites
against a local SQLite index) - there is no 'not applicable' category to
apply here, including cmd/rippleextract, which is an offline batch tool
but still queries the live Percona cluster.
Rules match on file plus optional function, or pin a single site by id
where more than one site shares a function and needs a distinct porting
note (digest_simulator.go's handleDigestSimulator, rippleextract's main).
This file is independent of tools/orm-migration/keep-raw.json - it does
not share ids or state with it.

rules.reason: Two-table JOIN session lookup with no MySQL-only functions - the closest thing in this service to a mechanical ORM candidate (wave 4), but converting one isolated site is not worth adding a GORM dependency to a service that has none. Deferred alongside the rest of this service's inventory.
rules.porting: No change required for PostgreSQL: ANSI INNER JOIN/WHERE/LIMIT, no MySQL-only syntax.
rules.category: Mechanical, deferred (no GORM in this service)

rules.reason: Two-table JOIN COUNT - same wave-4 mechanical shape and same deferral reason as middleware.go's jwtAuthMiddleware.
rules.porting: MySQL NOW() - INTERVAL 90 DAY -> PostgreSQL NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days' (the interval must be a quoted string literal on Postgres, unquoted on MySQL). COUNT/JOIN are otherwise unchanged.
rules.category: Mechanical, deferred (no GORM in this service)

rules.reason: Nearest-postcode reverse-geocode lookup ordered by MySQL's ST_Distance_Sphere; a rewrite bug here would silently return the wrong place name for a given point.
rules.porting: MySQL POINT(lng,lat) -> PostGIS ST_MakePoint(lng,lat) (or ST_Point). MySQL ST_Distance_Sphere(geomA, geomB) -> PostGIS ST_DistanceSphere(geomA, geomB) - same semantics, great-circle distance in metres on a spherical-earth model, same two-geometry-argument signature. The BETWEEN bounding-box prefilter is unchanged, ANSI SQL.

rules.reason: Spatial containment query against messages_spatial; core to member-area post retrieval, high blast radius if silently wrong.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_Contains(geomA, geomB) and ST_GeomFromText(wkt, srid) are the identical function names and signatures; SRID 3857 (Web Mercator) is supported identically. ST_X/ST_Y are unchanged. No other MySQL-only syntax.

rules.reason: Simulator-only endpoint, but shares the same `groups` spatial-containment shape as the live nearby-groups queries in groups.go; kept-raw for consistency with those rather than converted in isolation.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_AsGeoJSON, ST_Contains, ST_GeomFromText are identical function names and signatures. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted or double-quoted "groups" (not a Postgres reserved word).

rules.reason: Large multi-join simulator query mixing spatial containment with several correlated subqueries (view/reply counts, thumbnail attachment, outcome flags); genuinely hard to express as a single mechanical ORM chain without materially changing its shape - the kind of site plan 7.5 describes.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_X/ST_Y/ST_Contains/ST_GeomFromText are unchanged. Backtick-quoted identifiers (`groups`, the a.`primary` column alias) -> double-quoted ("groups", a."primary"). The EXISTS/correlated-subquery structure is unchanged, ANSI SQL.

rules.reason: The core nearby-groups query: a spatial containment test plus a centroid-distance fallback and an ORDER BY combining both; a rewrite bug here would silently reorder or drop groups a member should see.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_Contains, ST_GeomFromText, ST_Centroid, ST_Distance, ST_X/ST_Y are all identical function names and signatures. MySQL CONCAT('POINT(', ?, ' ', ?, ')') -> PostgreSQL CONCAT(...) works identically (Postgres's CONCAT has been variadic since 9.1), or better, switch to ST_MakePoint(?, ?) directly and drop the WKT string-building entirely. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted/double-quoted.

rules.reason: Single-group boundary/centroid lookup used to seed the routing graph; small, but on the graph-build path.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_AsText, ST_Centroid, ST_X, ST_Y are unchanged. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted/double-quoted.

rules.reason: Public groups-list endpoint; centroid computation only, no containment test.
rules.porting: PostGIS: ST_Centroid, ST_X, ST_Y are unchanged. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted/double-quoted.

rules.reason: The most MySQL-specific statement in this service: a STRAIGHT_JOIN optimizer hint plus an MBRContains bounding-box prefilter and an exact ST_Contains check combined. The join-order hint has no direct Postgres equivalent, so this needs a human decision at Phase 4, not a mechanical rewrite.
rules.porting: STRAIGHT_JOIN has no PostgreSQL equivalent - Postgres's planner does not take join-order hints without the third-party pg_hint_plan extension; drop the hint, rely on Postgres's planner and appropriate indexes, and re-check the plan with EXPLAIN after porting. MBRContains(bbox, geom) -> PostGIS: the `&&` bounding-box overlap operator against a GiST index, or ST_Intersects for an exact equivalent. ST_Contains/ST_GeomFromText/ST_SRID are unchanged. POINT(lng,lat) -> ST_MakePoint(lng,lat). NOW() - INTERVAL 90 DAY -> NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days'. Backtick-quoted `groups` -> unquoted/double-quoted.

rules.reason: Offline batch data-extraction tool for the ripple simulator (not the HTTP service, but still queries the live Percona cluster directly); enumerates candidate post IDs via a correlated EXISTS subquery (q1). The SQL text is static - only the one bind value (cutoff date) varies - so despite being read from a `q1` variable rather than a string literal, there is no dynamic query-shape risk in this particular statement.
rules.porting: No change required for PostgreSQL: ANSI INNER JOIN/EXISTS/IN, no MySQL-only syntax.

rules.reason: Same tool as q1 above; fetches post metadata in batches of up to 500 ids (q2), with the IN-list built at runtime via strings.Join over one `?` placeholder per id - a genuine variable-arm builder, the same shape that repeatedly stayed raw during iznik-server-go's own conversion (plan 7.5) because the placeholder count is not fixed at compile time.
rules.porting: MySQL DATE_FORMAT(x, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') -> PostgreSQL TO_CHAR(x, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'). MySQL IFNULL(x, y) -> PostgreSQL COALESCE(x, y). REPLACE(l.name, ' ', '') is ANSI-portable and unchanged. The hand-built IN (?,?,...) placeholder list should become a single = ANY($1) parameter bound to a Postgres array (pgx/lib/pq both support this) rather than porting the string concatenation as-is.

rules.reason: Same tool, same batch loop and same runtime-built IN-list shape as q2 above (q3), fetching repliers for the sampled posts.
rules.porting: MySQL DATE_FORMAT(x, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') -> PostgreSQL TO_CHAR(x, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS'). Same IN (?,?,...) -> = ANY($1) array-parameter note as q2 above applies here too.
